_meta.scenario: <think>/</think> routing under EVERY re-framing of the content-field pieces (incl. unterminated block, non-Latin scripts, F17 fenced-code literals)
_meta.semantics: pieces = the delta.content slices a single text arrives as (splitAtChar = boundary; -1 = the hand-written multi-piece delimiter framing). expected = atomic single-piece routing. Routing is CONTENT-scoped, so every re-framing must equal the atomic result: mismatchSplitChars must be EMPTY (chunking-invariance law). Think text lands in `reasoning`; an unterminated tail SURVIVES there (the pre-2026-11-13 scrubber deleted it — retired).
_meta.notes: Fence texts (added 2026-11-15 F17): a `<think>` inside a fenced code block is LITERAL text of the current channel, so for THOSE texts the channels legitimately contain delimiter spellings — the Rust replay's leak assertion is therefore scoped to fence-free texts. Shape changed 2026-11-13 (brief §2): the old byte-level upstreamStream/expectedRust scrub matrices are gone with ThinkScrubber. Rust replays each case through ThinkFieldSplitter (crates/ruke-server/tests/scrubber_vectors.rs). Texts are BMP-only: char-index slices must never split a surrogate pair (a lone half cannot be serialized in JSON); non-BMP coverage is pinned at BYTE level in fixture 03.
